title: Set 178

sentences.ko: 토요일에 차 몰고 호수에 가려고 했는데, 형 차가 시동이 안 걸려서 오전 내내 견인차만 기다리다가 결국 형네 집에서 피자나 먹었어.
sentences.text: We were going to drive up to the lake on Saturday, but my brother's car wouldn't start, so we spent the whole morning waiting for a tow truck and ended up just getting pizza at his place.

alts.text: Saturday we were gonna head up to the lake, but my brother's car wouldn't start. Spent the whole morning waiting on a tow truck and just ended up getting pizza at his place.
We had planned to drive up to the lake on Saturday; however, my brother's car would not start, so we spent the entire morning waiting for a tow truck and ultimately had pizza at his home.

sentences.note: **wouldn't start** 는 차가 시동이 안 걸린다는 말이에요. **ended up** 은 계획과 달리 결국 그렇게 됐다는 뜻으로 일상에서 아주 많이 써요.

sentences.ko: 그냥 싼 헤드폰 살 걸 그랬어. 이거 소리는 끝내주는데 너무 무거워서 한 시간 넘게는 못 쓰겠어. 그것도 300달러나 주고 샀는데.
sentences.text: I should've just gotten the cheaper headphones. These ones sound amazing, but they're so heavy I can't wear them for more than an hour, and I paid like three hundred bucks for them.

alts.text: Ugh, should've gone with the cheaper headphones. These sound amazing, but they're so heavy I can't wear them more than an hour, and I paid like three hundred bucks.

I should have purchased the less expensive headphones. These sound excellent, but they are so heavy that I cannot wear them for more than an hour, and I paid approximately three hundred dollars for them.

sentences.note: **should've just gotten** 은 그냥 ~할 걸 그랬다는 후회예요. **bucks** 는 dollars 를 편하게 부르는 말이고, 앞의 **like** 는 대충 그 정도라는 느낌을 줘요.

sentences.ko: 응, 엄마, 밥 잘 먹고 있어, 진짜야. 요즘 일이 좀 정신없어서 그래. 전화 못 한 건 그것 때문이야. 별일 없어.
sentences.text: Yeah, Mom, I'm eating fine, I promise. Work's just been kind of crazy, that's the only reason I haven't called. Nothing's wrong.

alts.text: I swear I'm eating fine, Mom. Work's just been nuts, that's the only reason I haven't called. Everything's okay.
Yes, Mother, I am eating well, I promise. Work has simply been very hectic, and that is the only reason I have not called. Nothing is wrong.

sentences.note: **kind of crazy** 는 좀 정신없다는 뜻이에요. 끝의 **Nothing's wrong** 은 걱정하는 사람에게 별일 없다고 안심시킬 때 써요.
sentences.situation: 부모님 안부 전화에서 잘 지낸다고 둘러대기

sentences.ko: 이번엔 다이어트를 목요일까지 버텼는데, 누가 회사에 도넛을 사 왔어. 딱 하나만 먹자고 했는데 결국 세 개나 먹어서, 아무래도 월요일부터 다시 시작해야겠어.
sentences.text: I lasted till Thursday on my diet this time, but then somebody brought donuts into work, and I told myself I'd just have one, and I ended up having three, so I guess I'm starting over on Monday.

alts.text: Made it to Thursday on the diet this time, but then somebody brought donuts to work. Told myself just one, ended up eating three, so I guess I'm starting over Monday.

This time I maintained my diet until Thursday, but then someone brought donuts into the office. I told myself I would have only one, and I ended up having three, so I suppose I will be starting over on Monday.

sentences.note: **lasted till Thursday** 는 목요일까지 버텼다는 말이에요. **starting over** 는 처음부터 다시 시작한다는 뜻이에요.

sentences.ko: 요즘 계란값 봤어? 예전엔 일주일 장을 60달러 정도면 봤는데, 지금은 똑같은 걸 사도 100달러가 나와.
sentences.text: Did you see how much eggs are now? I used to get groceries for the whole week for like sixty bucks, and now I'm spending a hundred and I'm still buying the same stuff.

alts.text: Have you seen egg prices lately? I used to get a whole week of groceries for like sixty bucks, and now it's a hundred for the same stuff.

Have you noticed how expensive eggs have become? I used to purchase groceries for the entire week for approximately sixty dollars, and now I am spending one hundred dollars while still buying the same items.

sentences.note: **Did you see how much eggs are now?** 는 요즘 계란이 얼마나 하는지 봤냐는 말로, 물가에 놀랄 때 써요. **the same stuff** 는 똑같은 것들이라는 편한 말이에요.

reviewed: 2번 한국어: '한 시간 넘게 못 쓰고 있어'는 영어(can't wear them for more than an hour, 쓸 수가 없다)와 뜻이 어긋나고, '그런데 ~줬다니까'는 앞말과 이어지는 맛이 어색해서 '한 시간 넘게는 못 쓰겠어. 그것도 300달러나 주고 샀는데.'로 고침
